slides.stem: For all values of $x$, $(x + 2)^3 = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$, where $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ are constants. What is the value of $a - b + c - d$?

slides.intro: Alternating signs is the fingerprint of $x = -1$.
steps: Flip the sign: $a - b + c - d = -1$
slides.trapWhy: $-27$ comes from mixing up the substitution. $x = 1$ gives the plain sum; alternating signs need $x = -1$.

slides.title: Coefficient sums are substitutions
slides.body:
Sum of the coefficients: plug in $x = 1$. Alternating sum: plug in $x = -1$. Then match the sign of what you got to the combination the question asks for.

Expanding the cube gets the same answer in four times the time.
